instruction.name: armmtflag
instruction.description: Write selected ARM flags in ARMFLAGS from the corresponding bit positions in rd, as determined by mask. Only ARMFLAGS is modified.

operands.name: rd
operands.description: source bits for the selected flags

operands.name: mask
operands.description: flag-selection mask (0xf selects N, Z, C, V)

latencies.notes: Moving the flag register costs two cycles in either direction. Only the round trip is measurable: masked moves in both directions take 4.00 cycles, and the cross-checks agree, `x86add.b rj, rk; x86mfflag rd, 1` and `adc.b rd, rj, rk; x86mtflag rd, 1` both read 4.00 as well, so every flag path in the LBT units - the two moves, the flag write of `x86add` and the carry-in of `adc` - is 2 cycles. The split rests on that convention: the totals only give m + n = e + n = b + m = e + b = 4, so 3 + 1 and 1 + 3 fit as well, but 2 + 2 is the assignment that matches the 2-cycle read-modify-write path measured on the flag read-write instructions.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: armmtflag $r4, 0xf; armmtflag $r5, 0xf; armmtflag $r6, 0xf; armmtflag $r7, 0xf; armmtflag $r8, 0xf; armmtflag $r9, 0xf; armmtflag $r10, 0xf; armmtflag $r11, 0xf
throughput.init: addi.d $r4, $r0, 1; addi.d $r5, $r0, 2; addi.d $r6, $r0, 3; addi.d $r7, $r0, 4; addi.d $r8, $r0, 5; addi.d $r9, $r0, 6; addi.d $r10, $r0, 7; addi.d $r11, $r0, 8; armmtflag $r0, 0xf
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 10000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --init 'addi.d $r4, $r0, 1; addi.d $r5, $r0, 2; addi.d $r6, $r0, 3; addi.d $r7, $r0, 4; addi.d $r8, $r0, 5; addi.d $r9, $r0, 6; addi.d $r10, $r0, 7; addi.d $r11, $r0, 8; armmtflag $r0, 0xf' --asm 'armmtflag $r4, 0xf; armmtflag $r5, 0xf; armmtflag $r6, 0xf; armmtflag $r7, 0xf; armmtflag $r8, 0xf; armmtflag $r9, 0xf; armmtflag $r10, 0xf; armmtflag $r11, 0xf'
throughput.notes: 8 independent lanes take 16.00 cycles, i.e. 2 CPI. The instruction is a single uop; its conditional execution limits it to one per two cycles (armmfflag and armmove are not conditional on register data and run at one per cycle). Re-measured on 2026-11-17 on LA664, core 0, with --method slope (--unroll 250 --unroll2 1000) and confirmed with the 0x01 uop counter.

notes: Latency 3 cycle(s) and throughput 2 CPI for the operand combination(s) recorded above, measured with ./bench on LA664.
